playwright_domain_readable_specs.instructions: Do multi-step Playwright specs express user-visible domain behavior clearly by encapsulating repeated DOM/Playwright mechanics behind thin injected fixtures or domain drivers while keeping `expect(...)` assertions visible in the spec?

criteria.pass: Multi-step user-journey specs read in problem-domain vocabulary (for example `coordinator.openPendingCase(...)`, `coordinator.approveCase(...)`) by delegating repeated locator chains, form fills, and browser event wiring to small focused fixtures (`test.extend`) or composed domain helpers/drivers, while keeping `expect(...)` assertions directly in the `.spec.ts` file (such as against returned domain values or `Locator` getters). Short, direct single-screen smoke tests (for example 5–10 lines verifying a route renders a heading or redirect) pass without needing a driver wrapper, as do small focused component/screen drivers without deep inheritance. Supporting fixture, driver, or config files without multi-step raw spec plumbing also pass.
criteria.fail: Multi-step E2E specs drown business behavior in dozens of raw `page.getByRole(...).filter(...).click()` / `.fill()` / `waitForEvent` plumbing lines across repeated tests so a reader cannot see the behavior under test; OR specs hide all assertions inside opaque Page Object methods (`await pageObj.verifyEverything()`) leaving the test body assertion-free; OR the suite builds speculative Selenium-style `BasePage` inheritance hierarchies or 1-to-1 kitchen-sink Page Objects for single-use screens.

playwright_isolated_fast_setup.instructions: Does the suite keep tests fast and parallel-safe by reusing authentication (`storageState`) and seeding preconditions via API/fixture helpers with teardown rather than serial test chains, shared mutable state, or repetitive UI setup flows?

criteria.pass: Tests run independently in parallel with isolated unique data created via fast API or database fixtures (`test.extend` with cleanup after `await use(...)`) and preloaded auth (`storageState` setup projects or role fixtures). Auth specs explicitly clearing `storageState` (`{ cookies: [], origins: [] }`) to test login or logout itself pass cleanly.
criteria.fail: Tests depend on execution order via `test.describe.serial` or module-level mutable variables (`let createdId`) passed from test A to test B; OR post-auth feature specs repeatedly click through full UI login forms or invoke multi-step UI creation wizard helpers before unrelated feature tests (such as upload or edit specs) instead of seeding preconditions via API/fixture; OR tests create manual browser contexts or shared records without fixture cleanup.

playwright_web_first_and_race_free.instructions: Do specs and helpers use auto-retrying web-first assertions and race-free Playwright synchronization rather than one-shot DOM snapshots, legacy ElementHandle APIs, arbitrary sleeps, `force: true` bypasses, or action-before-listener races?

criteria.pass: Assertions on DOM state use awaited web-first matchers (`await expect(locator).toBeVisible()`, `toHaveText`, `toHaveCount`, `toHaveURL`) and strict Locator actions; event listeners (`page.waitForEvent('download'|'popup')`, `page.waitForResponse(...)`) are armed before triggering the click/action (or via `Promise.all`); static checks on HTTP responses (`res.status()`), download filenames, parsed JSON, and `expect.poll()`/`toPass()` for non-DOM async checks pass cleanly. Fixture or helper files that perform no DOM assertions or browser synchronization also pass.
criteria.fail: Code uses one-shot non-retrying DOM snapshots (`expect(await loc.isVisible()).toBe(true)`, `textContent()`, `count()`), legacy ElementHandle or selector-string APIs (`page.$`, `page.$$`, `page.waitForSelector`, `page.click(sel)`), unawaited Playwright assertions or actions, arbitrary fixed sleeps (`page.waitForTimeout`), `waitForLoadState('networkidle')` as a UI-readiness crutch, `force: true` bypassing actionability, or triggers `.click()` before starting `waitForEvent`/`waitForResponse`.

playwright_strict_scoped_locators.instructions: Do specs and drivers locate elements via accessible user-facing roles/labels and semantic container/filter scoping rather than brittle CSS/XPath chains, positional `.nth()`/`.first()` crutches, or test-ID overuse?

criteria.pass: Locators prioritize `getByRole`, `getByLabel`, `getByPlaceholder`, and `getByText` scoped through semantic containers (`row.getByRole('button', ...)`, `.filter({ hasText })`, `dialog.getByRole(...)`). Intentional `.first()`/`.last()` assertions verifying sort order and `getByTestId` on genuinely non-semantic widgets (charts, canvases, layout shells) pass cleanly. Files that do not construct DOM locators also pass.
criteria.fail: Locators rely on CSS class/descendant chains (`.row-actions > div button`), CSS attribute or ID selector crutches (`page.locator('[aria-expanded="true"]')`, `page.locator('[id="..."]')`, `page.locator('#field-id')`, `page.locator('label input[type="file"]')`), XPath, `:nth-child`, positional `.nth(2)`/`.first()` crutches to target a specific domain record instead of scoping by row/filter, or `getByTestId` on standard buttons, links, inputs, or headings that have accessible roles and names.

playwright_honest_app_boundaries.instructions: Do Playwright specs exercise the real frontend–backend boundary without mocking away first-party APIs on happy paths via `page.route` or mutating internal app state via `page.evaluate`?

criteria.pass: Happy-path E2E specs exercise real app routes, loaders, and backend persistence (verifying real outcomes such as reload persistence or server state) against the configured test server or emulator. Targeted `page.route` usage strictly for fault injection (such as 500/503/offline/timeout error states) or external third-party hosts/widgets, browser storage cleanup (`localStorage.clear()`), and `request` API calls for test setup or server-state verification pass cleanly—including in spec files dedicated to error-handling or storage behavior.
criteria.fail: Happy-path E2E specs intercept first-party app APIs (`page.route('**/api/**', r => r.fulfill(...))`) with hardcoded fake success JSON so the real server/persistence path never executes; OR use `page.evaluate` to poke internal React/store globals or bypass real user interactions. Do NOT fail targeted `page.route` fault injection (5xx/error/timeout responses), external third-party domain stubbing, or `localStorage.clear()`.

playwright_suite_and_config_diagnostics.instructions: Do Playwright configuration (`playwright.config.*`) and suite files enforce CI safety (`forbidOnly`, `baseURL`, failure traces) without masking flakes through excessive unconditional retries, bloated timeouts, hardcoded URLs, contradictory serial-worker settings, or unreasoned skips?

criteria.pass: `playwright.config.*` sets `forbidOnly: !!process.env.CI`, bounds retries to CI (for example `retries: process.env.CI ? 1 : 0` or `2 : 0`), captures traces/artifacts on failure or retry (`trace: 'retain-on-failure'` or `'on-first-retry'`), centralizes `use.baseURL`, allows local parallel execution (Playwright's official default CI-only worker throttling `workers: process.env.CI ? 1 : undefined` alongside `fullyParallel: true` passes cleanly), and keeps test timeouts proportional (normal `webServer.timeout` is fine). Specs navigate with relative paths against `baseURL` without committed `test.only` or unreasoned `test.skip()` rot; explicit conditional skips (`test.skip(cond, 'clear reason')`) pass.
criteria.fail: Config omits `forbidOnly`, sets excessive unconditional retries (`retries: 3+` locally and in CI), sets huge test timeouts (`180_000+`) to hide hangs, disables failure traces (`trace: 'off'`), forces unconditional `workers: 1` (especially paired with `fullyParallel: true`) serializing the suite everywhere without explicit single-resource justification (do NOT fail CI-only `workers: process.env.CI ? 1 : undefined`), hardcodes absolute localhost or host URLs (such as `localhost:5173/...`) across specs instead of `baseURL`, or contains committed `test.only` or unreasoned `test.skip()` rot.
